name: Luxembourg
summary: A small grand duchy, independent since 1839 (neutrality guaranteed in 1867), a founder of the European communities and a major financial centre.

knownFor.label: European institutions
knownFor.note: Hosts the EU Court of Justice.

knownFor.label: Fortress of Luxembourg
knownFor.note: Old city walls, a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Free public transport
knownFor.note: First country with free public transport.

location.value: Western Europe between Belgium, France and Germany; 2,586 km².

terrain.value: The wooded Ardennes hills (Oesling) in the north, and the farmland and river valleys of the Gutland in the south, including the Moselle.

climate.value: Temperate and mildly oceanic, with mild summers, cool winters and rain spread through the year.

resources.value: Iron ore (minette) in the south, mined from the 1800s until 1981, plus farmland and Moselle vineyards.

disasters.value: No major natural disasters; floods along rivers such as the Sûre and Alzette, as in July 2021, and storms occur.

urbanisation.value: Luxembourg City, the capital, has about 135,000 people; Esch-sur-Alzette is the second town.

disease.value: Very good public health and long life expectancy, of more than 80 years.

migration.value: About 47% of permanent residents (2025) are foreign nationals.

economicBase.value: Services, especially banking and finance, produce most of the output; it is the world’s second-largest investment fund centre after the United States, and GDP per capita is the highest in the world (about $155,700 nominal in 2026). Steel is not covered in the part read.

tradeRoutes.value: Part of the EU single market and the Schengen area; the Schengen Agreement was signed in Luxembourg in 1985.

wealth.value: One of the richest countries per person.

moneyAndTax.value: The euro since 1999 (notes and coins from 2002); before that the Luxembourg franc, tied to the Belgian franc.

inequality.value: Fairly low inequality by world standards, but high housing costs create gaps between residents.

governmentType.value: A unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy, a representative democracy headed by Grand Duke Guillaume V.

keyRulers.value: The head of state is a hereditary grand duke; individual rulers are not named here.

institutions.value: The 60-seat Chamber of Deputies, the Council of State, the government led by a prime minister, and the grand duke.

stability.value: Stable in peacetime, but occupied by Germany in both World Wars (1914–18 and 1940–44).

eliteConflict.value: Little conflict among leaders; politics is based on coalitions, often led by the Christian Social People’s Party.

armyAndTech.value: A small volunteer army of under 1,000 soldiers; a founding member of NATO (1949).

majorWars.value: Invaded by Germany in August 1914 (First World War) and on 10 May 1940 (Second World War); liberated in 1944–45.

territoryChange.value: Lost its western, French-speaking part to Belgium in 1839; its borders have not changed since.

alliancesRivals.value: Founding member of the UN, the European Communities, OECD, NATO (April 1949) and Benelux.

inventions.value: Few major inventions; the country is known for steel making and later for satellite broadcasting through SES (founded 1985).

scienceEducation.value: High education levels; the University of Luxembourg, the country’s first university, was founded in 2003.

openness.value: Very open: many workers commute daily from France, Belgium and Germany, and most trade is with the EU.

communicationTransport.value: Free public transport since 29 February 2020, the first country to introduce it.

religion.value: 2021: 53% Christian, including 46% Catholic; collecting religious statistics has been illegal since 1980.

languageWriting.value: Luxembourgish is the sole national language; French is the sole language for legislation. In the 2021 census, 48.9% of citizens gave Luxembourgish as their main language.

artsArchitecture.value: The old town and fortifications of Luxembourg City (World Heritage since 1994) and castles such as Vianden.

socialStructure.value: A prosperous society with a large middle class; nearly half of residents are foreign nationals, especially Portuguese.

sharedIdentity.value: The national motto “Mir wëlle bleiwe wat mir sinn” (“We want to remain what we are”) and the Luxembourgish language.

dailyLife.value: Apartments and houses; Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked pork with beans).

neighbours.value: Belgium to the west and north, Germany to the east and France to the south.

ideasReligions.value: Catholic traditions such as the Echternach dancing procession, mixed with French and German culture.

colonisation.value: Luxembourg had no colonies; before 1839 it was itself ruled in turn by Spain, Austria, France and the Netherlands.

riseSignals.value: Elevated to a Grand Duchy on 9 June 1815; full independence confirmed by the Treaty of London on 19 April 1839.

peakPeriod.value: Modern prosperity since the 1980s, as banking and EU institutions replaced steel.

declineSignals.value: No major decline; the steel crisis of the 1970s cut jobs before finance grew.

outcome.value: Still in existence as an independent grand duchy and a member of the European Union.
